title: Path With Minimum Effort
summary: You prepare for a hike by finding the path with the least effort from the start to the end of a grid, where effort is defined as the greatest height difference between any two consecutive cells on the path.
statement: You prepare for a hike by finding the path with the least effort from the start to the end of a grid, where effort is defined as the greatest height difference between any two consecutive cells on the path.
constraints: 1–100 rows and columns with positive heights.
Path effort is the maximum absolute height change along its four-neighbor steps; minimize that maximum from top-left to bottom-right.
hints: This is a shortest-path problem where extending a path combines cost by maximum instead of addition.
Run Dijkstra using each cell’s smallest known effort.
Pop the lowest effort cell, relax each neighbor with max(current effort, edge difference), and stop at the destination.
The minimax cost never decreases when a path is extended, so Dijkstra’s settled-node proof applies unchanged.
editorial: The minimax cost never decreases when a path is extended, so Dijkstra’s settled-node proof applies unchanged.

tests.explanation: A route along changes no larger than two reaches the destination.
A route with maximum change one winds around the high center.
